subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Barcodes and Scanning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Barcodes and Scanning.

hook.text: The first barcode scanned in a store was on Wrigley's gum in 1974. It changed how inventory is tracked forever.

buildup.text: Barcodes encode product data in scannable lines. Scanning at each touchpoint records movement in real time.

discovery.text: They reduce manual data entry errors from 1-in-300 to nearly zero and speed up receiving and shipping.

twist.text: Standard barcodes only identify the product type, not the individual item. That limits traceability.

climax.text: 2D barcodes and QR codes now store much more data—batch numbers, expiry dates, and origin information.

punchline.text: A simple barcode turned inventory chaos into order.

quiz.question: What was the first product scanned with a barcode?
